Subject: SOC 2 timeframe and point-in-time coverage question

Hi Vanessa,

We're finalizing vendor due diligence for Acuity Health. Our procurement team has a couple of quick questions about Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report before we move to the security questionnaire:

- Can you confirm the exact inclusive dates covered by the latest SOC 2 Type II report you provided? Our reviewers interpret the header as "period: 03/01/2025 - 08/31/2025" but need explicit confirmation that March 1 through August 31 (inclusive) are covered.
- We also need to know whether any controls in the report were evaluated as a point-in-time on a specific cutoff date (e.g., 06/30/2025 or 08/31/2025), and for which control families (access, change mgmt, etc.).
- Finally, if our contract term extends beyond 08/31/2025, is a bridge letter available that covers subsequent months while the next SOC cycle completes? If so, what is the usual turnaround and who signs it (Redwood vs. auditor)?

If it's helpful, we're aiming to complete the SOC/contract review by end of next week.

Thanks,

Hi Lauren — Rafael here from the compliance team. Apologies for the delayed reply; I pulled the original auditor workpapers to be precise. Answers below are intentionally specific to help your procurement/security reviewers.

1) Inclusive reporting period
The SOC 2 Type II report we issued covers the period from 2025-03-01 through 2025-08-31 inclusive. That means testing encompassed events and controls in that interval; language in the report (page 2: "Period Covered") confirms inclusive month boundaries.

2) Point-in-time testing (cutoff dates)
- Access provisioning and deprovisioning controls: point-in-time sample verification performed as of 2025-06-30.
- Change management controls (e.g., code promotion approvals and change logs): samples included events through 2025-08-31 and a discrete cut-over test executed on 2025-08-31.
- Physical/environmental controls: perimeter walkthroughs recorded on 2025-05-15 (documented as inspection dates).

Where a "point-in-time" check was used, the report's testing notes indicate the date next to the control class. If you need a control-level mapping for your SIG/CAIQ matrix, we can produce a short control-mapping spreadsheet.

3) Bridge letters
We can provide an auditor-signed bridge letter that attests to no material changes in control environment between 2025-09-01 and a client-specified cutoff (we frequently do 2025-11-30 or 2025-12-31). Process notes:
- We prepare a draft based on our production change logs and incident records.
- The bridge is then reviewed and signed by our external auditor, ClearLake Auditors (their signature is what most customers require).
- Typical turnaround is 5–10 business days after you confirm the desired coverage dates and any required control call-outs.

If you confirm the bridge date range and whether you need control-level calls (e.g., please reference access controls + change management), Monica will coordinate the evidence pull and submit to ClearLake.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Compliance & Trust
rafael_mendes@redwood.com
